page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre. Heading "EXERC. IIII." with subtitle in spaced capitals and italic lines below. Main text in one column of body type, with one marginal note at the right margin beside the first line ("Cap.5."). Page number at the foot right.

main_text.head: EXERC. IIII.
AN IN NATVRALI MISTO quatuor elementorum formæ per- siftent incorrupta?
main_text.p: Cap.5.Fernelius eodem libro primo de Abdi- tis rerum caufis, & libro Phyfiologiæ fecundo, in mifto corpore fubftantias elementorum integras remanere, Hippo- cratis & Ariftotelis authoritate nixus, pro- bare contendit. Verum an ipfius fententiæ faueant, adeò celebres uiri, ac medicinæ & philofophiæ principes primùm nobis per- fcrutari licet. Hippocratis autem uerba ut- cunq; à Fernelio immutata, è primo de Na- tura humana lib. defumpta, funt hæc. Quan- do(inquit)humanū corpus interit, neceffe eft, fingula ad fuam fecreta natura reuerti, humidum ad humidum, ficcum ad ficcum, frigidum ad frigidum, calidum ad calidum. Ex his Fernelius quatuor elementorū mun- di fubftantias in humano corpore confifte- re perperam colligit. Etenim uerborū Hip- pocratis hic fenfus eft. Corpus humanum quando interit, neceffe eft fingula, quæ in eo

page.notes: Doubtful: the first word of the last line may read "quando" with a damaged initial. Line-end "Ex his" is set as printed with a space. Printed "colligit.Etenim" and "hæc.Quan-" are run together in the printing and are kept as printed. "eo" at the foot right is a catchword. The marginal "Cap.5." is printed with a stop after the 5 and a flourish; transcribed as printed.
